ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Dorothea Lange Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for new fatigue, weakness, muscle pain, and falls 55 years after childhood polio; recent heartburn. Concerns: New tiredness and weakness, now in the good leg and the arms as well as the leg weakened by polio in childhood, with aching after work and two falls; Heartburn after meals and at night for three months; Wants to keep photographing in the field and fears having to give it up. [S]

tr.td: Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets (1000 mg) by mouth up to three times a day as needed for muscle aching, no more than 3000 mg a day
Two tablets up to every 8 hours as needed
Omeprazole 20 mg delayed-release oral capsule, one capsule by mouth 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, an eight-week trial for heartburn
One capsule once daily before breakfast
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 1000 units oral tablet, two tablets (2000 units) by mouth once daily
Calcium carbonate 500 mg chewable tablet, one or two tablets by mouth as needed for heartburn, no more than six tablets a day, while off omeprazole before the endoscopy
One or two tablets up to every 4 hours as needed
Zoledronic acid 5 mg in 100 mL intravenous infusion over at least 15 minutes once a year
Omeprazole 20 mg delayed-release oral capsule, one capsule by mouth before breakfast for eight weeks to heal esophagitis, then the lowest dose that controls symptoms
One capsule once daily before breakfast

tr.td: Nerve conduction studies of both legs and the right arm: normal sensory and motor responses; no neuropathy or entrapment

Needle electromyography: large, long-duration, polyphasic motor units with reduced recruitment in the right quadriceps, tibialis anterior, and gastrocnemius; milder chronic reinnervation in the left vastus lateralis and right deltoid, muscles not known to have been affected; occasional fibrillation potentials in the right tibialis anterior; no myopathic units and no decrement on repetitive stimulation
Bone density scan (DXA) of the lumbar spine and both hips, with vertebral fracture assessment: osteoporosis of the right femoral neck; no vertebral fracture
Seated spirometry: forced vital capacity 2.52 L (92 percent of predicted), FEV1/FVC 78 percent; normal
Home overnight pulse oximetry: mean oxygen saturation 94 percent, oxygen desaturation index 3 per hour, no sustained desaturation; no nocturnal hypoventilation or sleep apnea pattern
Outpatient physical therapy, twelve weeks: individualized non-fatiguing strengthening and aerobic training with rest days, warm-water exercise, gait and balance training, and energy conservation
Custom lightweight carbon-fiber ankle-foot orthosis for the right leg, fitted and adjusted, with a single-point cane for the left hand
Intravenous infusion of zoledronic acid 5 mg over 30 minutes, after checking calcium, vitamin D, and creatinine; tolerated

Upper endoscopy with biopsies, three and a half weeks off omeprazole, under moderate sedation at reduced doses with continuous oxygen saturation and carbon dioxide monitoring: Los Angeles grade B esophagitis; 2 cm sliding hiatal hernia; regular squamocolumnar junction with no columnar-lined esophagus (no Barrett's esophagus); stomach with healed changes of the earlier ulcer operation and no ulcer; gastric biopsies without Helicobacter pylori

list.item: New fatigue and slowly increasing weakness for about 18 months, in the left leg and both arms as well as the right leg weakened by polio at seven, with aching muscle pain after work and cold intolerance of the right leg; cause to be established: resolved, confirmed [S]

Post-polio syndrome (modified March of Dimes criteria met): new weakness of the left quadriceps and both shoulder girdles and increased weakness of the right leg, with fatigue, muscle pain, and cold intolerance, more than 50 years after paralytic polio with partial recovery and decades of stable function; nerve conduction normal; EMG chronic reinnervation in both legs and the right deltoid; other causes excluded: active, confirmed [S]
Heartburn and regurgitation after meals and at night for three months, three to four times a week; no difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting, bleeding, or anemia: resolved, confirmed [S]
Gastroesophageal reflux disease with Los Angeles grade B erosive esophagitis on upper endoscopy off proton pump inhibitor; no Barrett's esophagus: active, confirmed [S]
Small (2 cm) sliding hiatal hernia on upper endoscopy: active, confirmed [S]

Osteoporosis, worst at the right hip on the polio-weakened side (right femoral neck T-score -2.7; left -1.6; lumbar spine -1.8), with vitamin D insufficiency; no vertebral fracture on assessment; 10-year FRAX risk about 16 percent major osteoporotic and 4.5 percent hip: active, confirmed [S]
Two falls in the past year without injury, from catching the right foot: active, confirmed [S]
Surgery for severe stomach ulcers in her early fifties; no ulcer symptoms since; avoids nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: active, confirmed [S]

Acute-phase reaction two days after the first zoledronic acid infusion: fever to 38.1 °C, muscle and joint aching, and headache, without signs of infection; calcium normal; resolved in three days with acetaminophen and fluids: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Primary care visit for new fatigue, weakness, muscle pain, and falls 55 years after childhood polio; recent heartburn
Diagnosis of post-polio syndrome with the neuromuscular rehabilitation consultation the same day; bone density and spirometry
Review after eight weeks of pacing and physical therapy; first zoledronic acid infusion; planning endoscopy after heartburn returned off omeprazole
Endoscopy results and reflux treatment; post-polio syndrome follow-up
Six-month review of post-polio syndrome, falls, bone health, and reflux step-down

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Work-up of new weakness as a diagnosis of exclusion: blood count, chemistry, glucose and HbA1c, TSH, B12, vitamin D, calcium, creatine kinase, ESR and CRP today; nerve conduction studies and needle EMG; PHQ-9; sleep screen
Neuromuscular physical medicine and rehabilitation consultation, to confirm or exclude post-polio syndrome and plan exercise, orthoses, and work adaptations
Heartburn: lifestyle measures and an eight-week trial of omeprazole 20 mg before breakfast; endoscopy if alarm features appear or if symptoms return when it is stopped
Fall prevention: home hazard review, footwear, night lighting, rails on the garden path, and a bone density scan for a woman with a weakened limb and falls
Pain care: acetaminophen as needed, heat, pacing, and stretching; no nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs after her ulcer surgery

Energy conservation and pacing: plan field days with rest breaks, a lighter camera and a harness instead of a shoulder bag, a seat stick, an assistant to carry the tripod, and a rest day after each field day; stop activity before fatigue
Supervised non-fatiguing exercise for twelve weeks (strengthening at submaximal effort with rest days, aerobic training, warm-water exercise, gait and balance training), then a home program
Custom lightweight carbon-fiber ankle-foot orthosis for right foot drop and knee instability, and a cane in the left hand; reassess for a knee-ankle-foot orthosis if knee buckling continues
Respiratory and sleep assessment: baseline spirometry and home overnight oximetry, with yearly spirometry and earlier review for breathlessness, morning headache, or swallowing trouble

Osteoporosis: vitamin D3 2000 units daily and dietary calcium; zoledronic acid 5 mg yearly once vitamin D is replete, given intravenously because of active reflux symptoms; DXA in two years; secondary-causes tests including a 24-hour urine calcium

Sedation and anesthesia precautions for post-polio syndrome recorded in the chart: reduced sedative and opioid doses, continuous oxygen and carbon dioxide monitoring, keep warm, careful positioning of the weak leg, and caution with neuromuscular blocking drugs
Upper endoscopy after two to four weeks off omeprazole, because heartburn returned within days of stopping it, with an antacid as needed meanwhile; sedation precautions for post-polio syndrome

Grade B reflux esophagitis: omeprazole 20 mg daily for eight weeks, then step down to the lowest dose that controls symptoms; weight-neutral lifestyle measures, no meals within three hours of bed, head of the bed raised; no Barrett's surveillance after a negative examination
Find the cause of the new weakness and fatigue within four weeks, with other treatable causes excluded
Post-polio syndrome diagnosed at 16 days after the tests excluded thyroid disease, anemia, diabetes, B12 deficiency, neuropathy, and myopathy
No falls over the next six months
No falls since the orthosis and cane; Timed Up and Go 11.2 seconds
Keep working in the field at least two days a week, with planned rests, without exhaustion the next day
Working two field days a week with a lighter camera, a seat stick, and rest breaks
Establish the cause of the heartburn and control it on the lowest effective therapy
Endoscopy showed grade B esophagitis without Barrett's esophagus; omeprazole restarted, symptoms controlled
Replete vitamin D and start fracture-protective treatment
Vitamin D 34 ng/mL; first zoledronic acid infusion given
